description:
Advances: ancora.review

Severity: High (calibrated). BLOCKS THE EPIC PR.

Concrete failure: mix spec.check --base ecc5e24 exits non-zero with spec.check result=fail tier=branch errors=0 warnings=1. CI smoke runs mix spec.check --base origin/BASE_REF with no continue-on-error, which for a PR into main is that identical command, so the PR is red on 100 percent of runs.

Cause, not a tool bug: .spec/specs/ancora.review.spec.md changed by exactly one line across all 37 branch commits, status draft to status active. That is spec-meta, which ancora.derive.acknowledgment_is_substantive correctly refuses to count as acknowledgment, while about 1000 lines of review code landed under that untouched contract.

Fix lands ON this branch before the PR. Tracked as a work order because the orchestrator does not author spec contracts; this needs an implementer plus a cold verifier per the epic discipline.

Found by /ship-it preflight, critical review 2026-09-03, finding F1. Verified by execution twice.

comments.text:
Full detail from the /ship-it preflight.

Verbatim gate output at 5220686 (env-pinned 27.2 / 1.18.1-otp-27):

  [WARNING] ancora.review derived/growth - :: ancora.review: tests now call new functions: Ancora.Markdown.render/1, Ancora.Markdown.render/2, Ancora.Review.FindingsDelta.classify/2, Ancora.Review.FindingsDelta.classify/3, Ancora.Review.Html.render/1, Ancora.Review.build/2, Mix.Tasks.Spec.Review.run/1 - acknowledge them in the spec for this subject
  checked subjects=7 requirements=82 errors=0 warnings=1
  branch base=ecc5e24 changed_files=175 findings=39 (error=0 warning=1 info=38, info hidden)
  branch next=edit the affected spec or production code
  spec.check result=fail tier=branch errors=0 warnings=1
  ** (Mix) spec.check failed

The CI command it maps to (.github/workflows/ci.yml, smoke step):
  base_ref="${PR_BASE_REF:-$DEFAULT_BRANCH}"
  git fetch --no-tags --depth=1 origin "$base_ref"
  mix spec.check --base "origin/$base_ref"
For a PR into main, base_ref=main and origin/main will be ecc5e24, so CI runs the exact failing command.

Why the epic never caught this: every per-ticket gate ran --base against a recent incremental base (26e3100 and similar), never against the actual PR base. Six of seven subjects received substantive requirement or scenario edits during the epic and cleared their growth findings; ancora.review is the only subject whose contract went untouched while its implementation landed.

Deliverable: a substantive requirement/scenario pass over .spec/specs/ancora.review.spec.md describing what actually shipped, covering the seven bindings above. NOT a Spec-Ack: trailer and NOT a config demotion - ancora.decision.slimmed_governance scopes trailers to mass mechanical edits, and this is the opposite case (real new surface, genuinely undescribed).

Verification:
- env ASDF_ERLANG_VERSION=27.2 ASDF_ELIXIR_VERSION=1.18.1-otp-27 mix spec.check --base ecc5e24  ends spec.check result=pass
- mix compile --warnings-as-errors, mix format --check-formatted, mix deps.unlock --check-unused
- full suite green on both CI matrix legs (1.18.4/OTP 26.2.5 and 1.19.5/OTP 28.3.1)

Sequencing: consolidated finding F41 (delete dead SpecDiff.compute/3, parse_source/1, FindingsDelta.compute/3 and the binary clause of classify/3) changes the function set ancora.review tagged tests call. Sequence F41 after this spec pass, or fold both into one change.

Allowed touches: .spec/specs/ancora.review.spec.md, plus .spec/decisions/** only if an ADR is genuinely required.
Out of scope: weakening the acknowledgment mechanism; behavior changes under lib/ancora/review/**.

Consolidated report: /Users/mz/vaults/rmbrs-vault/code_review/critical/ancora/2026-09-03/ancora-yzu-spec-anchored-successor/20260903-052243-consolidated.md

IMPLEMENTED
Session: ayj-impl-1
Log: /Users/mz/.local/state/agentic-runs/ancora/ancora-ayj/codex-ayj-impl-1/log

Commit: a47d0fe29dc08aa00693f00a96601d08b1650d94
Files touched: .spec/specs/ancora.review.spec.md, .spec/decisions/ancora.decision.review_artifact_contract.md, test/ancora/review_test.exs
Tests added: none; three existing production-builder tests gained the ancora.review.view_model_builder tag
Spec acknowledgment: substantive requirement/scenario edit to .spec/specs/ancora.review.spec.md — added the view-model builder requirement and drift, growth, and acknowledgment scenarios for Ancora.Review.build/2; amended the HTML view and output contracts for Ancora.Review.Html.render/1; defined exact list classification and clean-verdict behavior for Ancora.Review.FindingsDelta.classify/2 and classify/3; defined the GFM, wikilink, raw-HTML, and fallback behavior of Ancora.Markdown.render/1 and render/2; and made the success, usage-error, and output behavior of Mix.Tasks.Spec.Review.run/1 explicit.
Verification tier: change-scoped — mix compile --warnings-as-errors; mix format --check-formatted; mix deps.unlock --check-unused; test/ancora/review_test.exs; mix test --stale; mix spec.check against both required bases; full-system proof deferred to the merge gate / PR CI
Final-tier runs: 2
Gate vs ticket base cfc229f: spec.check result=pass
Gate vs main ecc5e24: before: spec.check result=fail tier=branch errors=0 warnings=1; after: spec.check result=pass
Full suite: 3 properties, 331 tests, 0 failures
Contract corrections: watched cards render the changed file's full diff rather than a clause-level hunk; supporting changes are remaining changed source files rather than footprint files; the green-chip scenario starts from a populated view model rather than an empty change set; renderer fallback is exercised through Markdown.render/2 and does not assert that the Mix task receives the injected renderer; the shipped Prism grammar is markup rather than html.

Summary: The review contract now names the public builder, classifier, markdown renderer, HTML renderer, and Mix task entry points and gives each observable behavior that existing tagged tests exercise. A new accepted ADR records the shipped boundaries and the corrections to the preimplementation spec, with no production behavior changes.

VERIFY: PASS (agent verify-ayj, opus, cold; relayed by the orchestrator — verdict delivered by teammate message in three parts)
Session: 68fab1f9-dfb5-49e0-be76-afa9d2d00f6d
Log: /Users/mz/.claude-personal/projects/-Users-mz-src-ancora/68fab1f9-dfb5-49e0-be76-afa9d2d00f6d.jsonl

Mechanical scope: 3 files — .spec/specs/ancora.review.spec.md, .spec/decisions/ancora.decision.review_artifact_contract.md, test/ancora/review_test.exs. Outside the ticket's written Allowed touches: 1 (the test file), covered by the orchestrator brief's explicit tag-addition authorization. The test diff is tag-only: three added lines, each the identical @tag spec: "ancora.review.view_model_builder" at lines 79, 115, 130; zero changes to assertions, setup, fixtures, or helpers.

Fake-green ruleout (the central risk on this ticket):
- Spec-Ack trailer: ABSENT. One commit in range (a47d0fe "docs(spec): describe shipped review surface"); its body is the subject line and nothing else.
- config.yml demotion: ABSENT. The diff against .spec/config.yml is empty.
- Vacuous requirements: none. Every new/amended clause has an assertion behind it, including the two the verifier expected to be filler (meta_line_shape's usage-failure clause at spec_review_test.exs:33-41; findings_delta_without_store's dedup and clean-verdict clauses at review_test.exs:70-75). One clause is genuinely UNTESTED but not unfalsifiable: output_flag's "--open shall ask the host to open the written file without turning a launcher failure into a task failure" — deleting the rescue at lib/mix/tasks/spec.review.ex:48-51 would break it. Minor.
- must weakened / ADR misuse: no mechanical downgrade — 9 must before, 10 after, no non-must requirements on either side. The ADR is legitimate: affects: [ancora.review] resolves (adr/affects_unresolved is error-severity, adr/affects_empty warning-severity, and the run reports errors=0 warnings=0, so both cleared); all three required sections present per decision_parser.ex:20; and its Consequences section DISCLOSES the downside rather than burying it ("Watched cards can repeat context outside the changed clause, and a subject's supporting section can contain source files outside that subject's derived bindings").

Contract corrections — the verifier read the code BEFORE the implementer's claims and ruled on each of five:
1. Watched cards render the full file diff, not a clause-level hunk — SPEC WAS WRONG. review.ex:181 and :205 both set lines: Map.get(diffs, file, []); there is no hunk-slicing anywhere in the module, and changed_definitions/2 reads diff lines only to name bindings. See the F16 note below.
2. Supporting = remaining changed source files, not footprint files — SPEC WAS WRONG, and this is the other half of the duplication. review.ex:137-143 derives supporting from the GLOBAL changed_files list for every subject, filtered only by source_file?/1 minus the subject's own spec file, changed tagged tests, and watched files. Nothing consults the derived footprint. Seven impacted subjects plus the all-files panel is the eight copies measured by the frontend review.
3. Green chip from a populated view model — SPEC WAS WRONG, no bug blessed. The old claim was achievable (an empty change set traces through gate_report/3 to verdict: :pass at review.ex:107) but was never how the test worked; the test at review_test.exs:13 hands Html.render/1 a hand-built and in fact impossible model (verdict: :pass beside an introduced derived/drift error). The rename is honest. Modest coverage loss: no test now walks empty-change-set to green chip end to end; the derivation is still proven at review_test.exs:75.
4. Fallback via Markdown.render/2 — SPEC WAS WRONG, no bug blessed. markdown.ex:12-24 takes a :renderer option and markdown_test.exs:26-32 injects a raising renderer. Awkwardness named: markdown.ex:14 calls :renderer "a test-only injection point" and the spec now promotes that seam to a must — truthful, but it contracts a test hook as public API.
5. Prism markup not html — SPEC WAS WRONG, trivially. The vendored file is prism-markup.min.js, which registers Prism.languages.markup and aliases html/xml/svg/mathml/rss/atom/ssml. Prism ships no prism-html.min.js, so the old spec named a file that cannot exist.

Tag honesty: all three honest, each landing on a different clause, with the killing mutation named — review_test.exs:80 (mutate binding_delta/2 at review.ex:276-285 to filter on the wrong finding code and added_bindings goes empty, failing line 105); :116 (mutate drift_cards/2 at review.ex:173-184 to emit a different badge or narrow the "derived/drift" filter, failing line 126); :131 (set watched_cards = drift_cards alone at review.ex:132, or break called_bindings/2 at :212-221, failing line 148 — this is the one that genuinely exercises the tagged-test-scan clause, since acknowledged cards only surface for bindings the tagged tests call).

Re-runs:
- spec.check --base cfc229f: spec.check result=pass (changed_files=3, findings=7, error=0 warning=0)
- spec.check --base ecc5e24: spec.check result=pass. checked subjects=7 requirements=83 errors=0 warnings=0 / branch base=ecc5e24 changed_files=175 findings=38 (error=0 warning=0 info=38). DISCRIMINATOR CONFIRMED on both halves: warnings=0 AND 38 findings rather than 39, so derived/growth is CLEARED, not relabeled to info.
- review_test.exs: 6 tests, 0 failures. Full suite: 3 properties, 331 tests, 0 failures.

Verdict: PASS. Gaps: none.

Notes — the F16 judgement, which the orchestrator asked for explicitly:
"This is honest contract-alignment whose side effect is retiring a live defect's written basis, and the orchestrator should treat those as two separate things. The implementer did not fake anything; every one of the five corrections is factually true of lib/ancora/review.ex as shipped, and the ADR states the cost in plain language. Given they were not told about F16, writing down what the code does is the right move, and failing this ticket would punish good-faith work for a defect it was never scoped to fix. But the cost is real: before this change F16 was a contract violation with a citable line; after it, F16 is a matter of taste. And nothing replaces the constraint — size_budget bounds renderer SOURCE lines, so after this merge no requirement in .spec/ constrains artifact size at all. The artifact could reach 50 MB and the gate would stay green."
Recommended re-base for F16 (verbatim): add a must to ancora.review alongside size_budget that bounds the rendered ARTIFACT rather than the renderer source — "the rendered artifact shall include each changed file's diff at most twice (once under the subject that owns it, once under All files), and shall stay under N MB for a change set of 200 files, enforced by a standing test" — paired with a scenario building a multi-subject fixture asserting per-file article count, so the test fails today and passes once supporting changes are scoped to the owning subject (the mechanism is review.ex:137-143). Note size_budget's own cut list already names the right lever ("supporting-changes hunks degrade to a file-link list"); it was simply wired to the source-line budget instead of an artifact budget.

Two smaller loose ends, both follow-ups (outside this ticket's Allowed touches):
- NOTICE:95 still reads "json, html, css, and javascript grammars only", so NOTICE and the spec now disagree on the grammar name, and review_assets_test.exs only checks NOTICE contains "PrismJS 1.29.0", so nothing catches the drift.
- The three new tags dual-label tests that already carried code_pivot_grouping, so coverage is re-labeled existing evidence. What makes the second tag honest is that these three go through Review.build/2 while the hand-built-model tests could not carry it — a real distinction but a thin one. The requirement would be better served by at least one test asserting on something only build/2 produces (meta, or outside_changes).

AUDIT: APPROVE
Session: 68fab1f9-dfb5-49e0-be76-afa9d2d00f6d
Log: /Users/mz/.claude-personal/projects/-Users-mz-src-ancora/68fab1f9-dfb5-49e0-be76-afa9d2d00f6d.jsonl

Reasoning: The scope seam is clean and I rule the expansion acceptable — `git diff --numstat cfc229f..a47d0fe -- test/ancora/review_test.exs` is exactly 3/0, and all three added lines are the identical `@tag spec: "ancora.review.view_model_builder"` at 79, 115, 130, with no assertion, setup, fixture, or helper touched, so the brief's tag-only authorization was not exceeded. Every other mechanical claim confirmed independently rather than inherited: 3 files, empty `.spec/config.yml` diff, commit body is the subject line alone with no `Spec-Ack:`, and 9 `must` at base against 10 at head with every requirement `must` on both sides and all 9 base ids still present, so neither `append_only.ex` guard event (`:36` requirement_deleted, `:50` must_downgraded, the latter firing only on must->should at `:66`) is in play at all. The five contract corrections are factually true of the shipped code and I traced the first two to source myself — `review.ex:181` and `:205` both set `lines: Map.get(diffs, file, [])`, the whole file diff, with no hunk slicing anywhere in the module, and `review.ex:137-143` derives `supporting` from the global `changed_files` filtered only by `source_file?/1` minus spec/changed-test/watched, never consulting the derived footprint — so "the spec was wrong" genuinely holds, and with `lib/ancora/review/**` explicitly out of scope the spec edit was the only in-scope resolution available. No `must` was weakened to bless a defect in the guard's sense, but `code_pivot_grouping` did get materially looser and that retires F16's citable written basis; the verifier named that cost and the re-base text in plain language instead of burying it, which is the right disposition for a defect this ticket was never scoped to fix. Tag honesty holds on all three: each test goes through `Review.build/2` and asserts a distinct clause that dies under the named mutation — `review_test.exs:105` dies if `binding_delta/2` (`review.ex:276`) filters the wrong code, `:126` dies if `drift_cards/2` (`review.ex:173`) changes the badge, `:148` dies if `watched_cards` (`review.ex:132`) drops `acknowledged_cards` or `called_bindings/2` (`review.ex:212`) breaks.

ADR ruling: legitimate, and NOT functioning as authorization to weaken a must. All three required sections present per `decision_parser.ex:20`, `affects: [ancora.review]` resolves to a real subject, and its Consequences discloses the duplication downside. It cannot be laundering a downgrade because no requirement was deleted and no priority moved.

Notes (escalated, not bounced — no execution environment here):
- `affects: ancora.review` is subject-scoped, and `append_only.ex:73-83` authorizes on requirement id OR subject id with no check that the ADR is about the specific change. So this accepted ADR now stands as blanket authorization for any future `append/requirement_deleted` or `append/must_downgraded` on every requirement in ancora.review, indefinitely. That is the designed mechanism (`no_execution_no_state` affects five subjects the same way), not this implementer's doing, but the blast radius is wider than this ADR needs and is worth a board item against the guard, not this ticket.
- Confirming the verifier's NOTICE finding: `NOTICE:95-96` still reads "json, html, css, and javascript grammars only" while `prism_carried` now says `markup`. The requirement stays true of the vendored file set (`priv/spec_review_assets/prism-markup.min.js`, no `prism-html.min.js` exists), and `review_assets_test.exs:16` only asserts NOTICE contains "PrismJS 1.29.0", so nothing catches the wording drift. Cosmetic, follow-up.
- F16 re-base is real and unaddressed: `size_budget` (spec :108-117) was untouched and still bounds renderer SOURCE lines, so after this merge nothing in `.spec/` bounds the rendered artifact. The verifier's recommended replacement requirement cannot land inside this ticket's Allowed touches, since by its own design the paired test must fail until `review.ex:137-143` scopes supporting changes to the owning subject, which is a `lib/ancora/review/**` behavior change this ticket forbids. Route it as its own ticket.

Mechanical-remedy bounce count this ticket (if any): 0/2

title: Acknowledge the shipped ancora.review surface so the gate passes against main
